commit_role: qualified code/test source; the exact publication HEAD is bound by the external verification request
design: Epoch-bound leases (LLD v1.1 section 1.4 lists stop_epoch in the CapabilityLease record; ADD v1.3 section 5.5 'Ogni mutative call presenta una capability lease con stop_epoch corrente'): CapabilityLease gains an optional stop_epoch; CapabilityAuthority can be bound to one stop controller (constructor or bind_stop_controller, rebinding to another controller refused); a bound authority stamps the controller's epoch on every lease after checking the controller is NORMAL at that epoch, and refuses issuance otherwise. Stop acceptance increments the epoch atomically (c6/safety.py unchanged), which revokes every lease of the previous epoch in the local boundary; a reset issues yet another epoch, so a pre-stop lease is never re-enabled.

ToolCallRuntime binds its authority to its controller at construction. After the existing capability, purpose and marking gates it requires the authoritative lease's stop_epoch, requires the presented stop_epoch to equal it (a command prepared before the stop is refused even with a fresh lease) and fences on it. The presented epoch is an assertion of the caller, never the authority.

Per-tool capability: the registered tools the expression can call are found by parsing it (only names registered in the sandbox; anything the sandbox would refuse is left to its own refusal, preserving the 0047 escape-syntax behaviour and budget charge), and each must be authorized by the lease before the budget is charged. Each dispatch re-authorizes (no use consumed) and re-fences.

Preemptive dispatch: StrictSandbox.execute accepts an optional dispatch hook receiving (name, call). The runtime runs the call on a daemon worker thread with a context variable naming the call, and supervises it every 10 ms: an accepted stop or the deadline sets the call's cancellation flag and refuses at once with execution_unknown; a stop accepted during a call that completes also refuses with execution_unknown. cancellation_checkpoint()/cancellation_requested() are the cooperative cancellation point (LLD v1.1 section 6) for tools.

Repair 1 (VF-001): each dispatch runs in a _ToolWorker. On an accepted stop or the deadline the supervisor sets the cooperative cancellation flag, waits at most 0.25 s, then schedules ToolPreempted (BaseException) once in the worker via PyThreadState_SetAsyncExc; the worker clears any pending one when it retires, under the same lock, so it is never scheduled in a retired thread whose id may be reused. The call is refused at once (STOP_BOUND_DENIED or TOOL_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, execution_unknown) as before.

Repair 1 (VF-002/VF-003): CapabilityAuthority bound to a controller fences authorize() itself (lease epoch must be present and current, controller NORMAL), requires the parent's epoch on delegation, and sweeps its ledger once per epoch change, recording superseded leases as revoked at the accepted stop (StopEpochAuthority now also exposes history; c6/safety.py unchanged).

Repair 2, reconciliation (REM-0027-REPAIR-2-SCOPE-AND-VF001-DISPOSITION point 1; ADD v1.3 section 5.5 points 5-6): ToolCallRuntime takes an optional C6 OutcomeReconciler (a real one is created when none is injected) and, before raising any execution_unknown refusal (stop accepted while a tool runs, call deadline, stop observed on completion), calls OutcomeReconciler.mark_ambiguous with a fresh command id, idempotent_effect_proven=False, the refusal instant and a canonical JSON note carrying lease_id, tool_name, stop_epoch, reason_code, correlation_id (from the GovernedContext), dispatched_at and refused_at. The returned ReconciliationRecord is wrapped in an UnknownToolOutcome that travels with the refusal (ToolRuntimeError.reconciliation) and is journalled by the runtime (unknown_outcomes). If the reconciler raises, the call fails closed with RECONCILIATION_UNAVAILABLE (execution_unknown, cause chained) and no receipt. c6/safety.py is not modified (the existing mark_ambiguous API is used), so REM-0024/REM-0028 surfaces are untouched.

Repair 2, lease channel (point 2): ToolCallRuntime.authorize_effect(lease, tool, subject, at) re-authorizes an effect of a tool on the bound CapabilityAuthority and maps StopEpochDenied to STOP_BOUND_DENIED and any other AuthorizationError to CAPABILITY_DENIED; an effect attempted after an accepted stop, including from a finally that runs late, is refused there.

Repair 2, documentation (point 3): the module docstring states that asynchronous preemption is best-effort between interpreter steps, that a running native call and the finally that follows it are not interruptible (the finally runs when the native call returns: measured 11.5 s after the stop for a 12 s native wait), what stays bounded (refusal <=10 s, no new dispatch, no usable pre-stop lease on the lease channel, reconciliation), and that the ungoverned-channel effect is a measured residual traced to FGM-17 and the G6 qualification.

findings_scope.C8-1: fixed: every tool dispatch of the expression is fenced against the controller's current epoch immediately before it runs (EmergencyStopController.guard_dispatch with the lease's epoch); a stop accepted after the entry gates refuses the first dispatch with STOP_BOUND_DENIED and no effect
findings_scope.C8-2: fixed: each tool call runs on a worker thread supervised every 10 ms; a stop accepted while it runs refuses the call at once (STOP_BOUND_DENIED, execution_unknown) and no later tool of the expression is dispatched; a cooperating tool is cancelled through cancellation_checkpoint before its effect and a non-cooperating one is preempted (repair 1, VF-001); a per-call deadline (default 5 s, at most the 10 s containment target) bounds any call with TOOL_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. Measured in the suite: return within the 10 s target from stop acceptance under an 11 s tool, no effect after the stop
findings_scope.C8-3: fixed: ToolCallRuntime binds its CapabilityAuthority to its EmergencyStopController; every lease records the trusted epoch at issuance (LLD v1.1 section 1.4 lists stop_epoch in the lease record), issuance is refused while the stop is not NORMAL, a lease of another epoch or of none never dispatches, the caller's stop_epoch is only compared with the lease's (never trusted), and a pre-stop lease cannot delegate after the reset
findings_scope.VF-001: fixed: a cancelled tool still running after a 0.25 s cooperative grace is preempted: ToolPreempted, a BaseException (an ordinary except Exception cannot swallow it), is scheduled once in its worker thread through CPython's PyThreadState_SetAsyncExc, serialized with the worker's retirement by a lock so it is never scheduled in a retired thread; the tool stops at its next interpreter step, before any effect that follows its blocking wait. The qualifying tests now journal a mutative effect with its monotonic timestamp and fail if any lands later than 10 s after the stop acceptance (non-cooperative stop case, deadline case, and a new non-cooperative tool with a broad except Exception, which is now preempted within the target instead of after its own 11 s).
findings_scope.VF-001 (verdict OCOR-DEV-REM-0027-5cb0f6: disposed by the Product Owner (REM-0027-REPAIR-2-SCOPE-AND-VF001-DISPOSITION, 2026-10-14): founded in fact, not blocking as formulated; the acceptance criterion is realigned to ADD v1.3 section 5.5. Repair 2 implements the closed scope: reconciliation of every execution_unknown (positive and fail-closed negative), the native wait + finally case with the effect journalled inside the finally (refusal within 10 s, execution_unknown with reconciliation record, lease-channel effect refused STOP_BOUND_DENIED, ungoverned effect measured as residual, never PASS), corrected docstring and evidence. Out-of-process tool execution is not authorized in this cycle and is recorded as a design option for the FGM-17 qualification in G6.
findings_scope.VF-002: fixed: on a bound authority a delegation whose child carries an epoch requires the parent's epoch to be present and equal (StopEpochDenied otherwise); the ledger sweep also records an epoch-less parent as revoked at the first accepted stop after the binding.
findings_scope.VF-003: fixed: authorize() on an authority bound to a controller refuses a lease bound to no epoch or to an epoch other than the current one, and every lease while the controller is not NORMAL (StopEpochDenied, an AuthorizationError, mapped by ToolCallRuntime to STOP_BOUND_DENIED); every caller of authorize() sharing the bound authority inherits the fence (tested through AgentKernel.execute_sandboxed). Once the controller moves past the epoch the ledger last saw, every lease of an older epoch is recorded as revoked at the accepted stop that superseded it (StopEvent.at of the activation), so the reset leaves no pre-stop lease active in the ledger.
findings_scope.class_check: every registered tool the expression can call must be covered by the lease: checked statically before anything is charged or run (no partial effect) and again at each dispatch (a lease revoked mid-expression stops the next tool)
findings_scope.unchanged: the five entry gates and their order and reason codes; receipts; StrictSandbox behaviour without the dispatch hook; CapabilityAuthority behaviour for authorities not bound to a stop controller (a bound authority now also fences authorize(), repair 1); EmergencyStopController (c6/safety.py byte-identical, so OCOR-DEV-0044 is not requalified and REM-0024 is not touched); public OpenAPI/proto contracts

measured_residuals.description: effect of a registered tool on a channel the platform does not govern, executed in the finally that follows a 12 s native wait, measured from the accepted stop; reported as measurement only, never as containment

normative_interpretations: ADD v1.3 section 5.5 target '<=10 s' is measured 'dall'accettazione locale dell'evento firmato all'ultimo nuovo command accettato': a tool dispatch is the new command accepted, and the fence makes every dispatch after the stop acceptance impossible; the call deadline is bounded by the same 10 s so no supervised call outlives the target without a refusal.

ADD v1.3 section 5.5 points 4-6 ('cancella operazioni in-flight quando il contract lo consente; avvia compensation o reconciliation per operazioni non cancellabili; EXECUTION_UNKNOWN agli effetti ambigui'): the sandbox tool contract is a plain callable, so in-flight cancellation is cooperative (cancellation_checkpoint); a non-cooperating call is abandoned with execution_unknown and its outcome is not inferred.
The per-call deadline default (5 s) follows the lease TTL bound of ADD v1.3 section 5.2/5.5 ('TTL non superiore a 5 secondi'); it is configurable up to the 10 s containment target and never above.

Acceptance criterion of repair 2 (PO disposition REM-0027-REPAIR-2-SCOPE-AND-VF001-DISPOSITION, a reading of ADD v1.3 section 5.5 and LLD v1.1 sections 4.3 and 6, not a semantic change): from the stop acceptance no new tool dispatch is accepted and no pre-stop lease is usable, measured <=10 s; an in-flight call is cancelled at cooperative checkpoints or closed by the deadline with execution_unknown; every execution_unknown outcome produces a reconciliation record. The previously recorded loop criterion 'last tool effect <=10 s' is superseded by this disposition.

The ungoverned-channel effect of a finally after a native wait is not claimed contained: it is measured (RESIDUAL_MEASURED_NOT_PASS) and traced to FGM-17 and G6; if the G6 campaign shows that the in-process residual violates 'nessuna tool influence successiva', a decision request is opened (PO disposition).

a stop accepted by a separate thread after every entry gate (inside the budget charge) or by the first tool of an expression refuses the next dispatch STOP_BOUND_DENIED: no effect, respectively only the effect of the tool that was already running (RED on 299a6a6: DID NOT RAISE, the effect landed after the stop)

measured with an 11 s MUTATIVE tool whose effect is journalled with its monotonic timestamp (repair 1, VF-001): a stop accepted 0.5 s into the call refuses it within the 10 s target from stop acceptance (STOP_BOUND_DENIED, execution_unknown) and no effect lands later than 10 s after the stop -- the non-cooperative tool is preempted before its effect, one that swallows ordinary exceptions is preempted within the target, a cooperating tool leaves through its own checkpoint (ToolCancelled, before any preemption) with no effect, the next tool of the expression never runs; a fast non-cooperative tool without stop still produces its effect (positive control); without a stop the per-call deadline (5 s default, 1 s configured) refuses TOOL_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED with no further effect; deadlines of 0, negative or above 10 s are refused (RED on 299a6a6: the call ran 11 s and the next tool produced its effect; deadline API absent; repair-1 RED on f48452c: the slow mutative effect landed 10.5-11 s after the stop)

a lease records the controller epoch at issuance; a pre-stop lease is refused after dual-control reset although the caller presents the current epoch, cannot delegate after the reset, and a fresh lease does not let a command fenced before the stop dispatch; no lease is issued during the stop; a lease bound to no epoch is refused; an authority cannot be rebound to another controller; a current-epoch lease still delegates; a pre-stop parent cannot delegate even with a child issuance backdated inside its life before the stop (repair 1, regression guard killing M14) (RED on 299a6a6: pre-stop lease accepted, no epoch recorded; the stale-command case is a regression guard that also passes there)

on an authority bound to the runtime's controller a parent lease issued before the binding (no epoch) cannot delegate, with or without an intervening stop and reset; a child of a current-epoch parent carries the same epoch and runs its tool (positive) (RED on f48452c: both epoch-less delegations DID NOT RAISE)

CapabilityAuthority.authorize() of the bound authority refuses a pre-stop lease after the reset, every lease while the controller is STOPPING or STOPPED and a lease bound to no epoch; the ledger records the pre-stop lease as revoked exactly at the accepted stop; a current-epoch lease is authorized after the reset (positive); AgentKernel.execute_sandboxed sharing the authority refuses the pre-stop lease and accepts a fresh one (RED on f48452c: authorize() and execute_sandboxed accepted the stale leases)

an expression calling a registered tool the lease does not cover is refused CAPABILITY_DENIED before anything is charged or run (no partial effect, budget 0); a lease revoked by the first tool refuses the second at its dispatch (RED on 299a6a6: both tools ran)

every execution_unknown refusal (stop accepted while a tool runs; call deadline) records, before it is raised, an EXECUTION_UNKNOWN outcome with the real C6 OutcomeReconciler, never idempotent-proven, whose note carries lease, tool, stop epoch, dispatch and refusal times, reason code and correlation; the record travels with the refusal and is journalled by the runtime; require_may_auto_retry refuses it (AUTO_RETRY_BLOCKED_AMBIGUOUS_NON_IDEMPOTENT); a completed call opens no reconciliation (positive control); the default runtime owns a real reconciler (RED on f34b46e: reconciler parameter and record absent)

a reconciler whose store is unreachable makes an execution_unknown call fail closed with RECONCILIATION_UNAVAILABLE (execution_unknown, cause chained, no receipt, no record, no effect, refusal within 10 s of the stop); a call that completes is unaffected (positive control)

a tool waiting in one native call (time.sleep 12 s) attempts its effect in its finally, journalled there: invoke refuses within 10 s of the stop (STOP_BOUND_DENIED, execution_unknown) with a C6 reconciliation record; the late effect attempted through the lease channel (ToolCallRuntime.authorize_effect on the bound authority) is refused STOP_BOUND_DENIED; the effect on an ungoverned channel is printed as a measured residual (RESIDUAL_MEASURED_NOT_PASS, see measured_residuals) and is never asserted as contained; the lease channel authorizes an effect without a stop and refuses one outside the lease (CAPABILITY_DENIED)

residual_risks: In-process preemption is best-effort between interpreter steps: a running native call (time.sleep, blocking I/O) and the finally that follows it are not interruptible; the finally runs when the native call returns (measured 11.5 s after the stop for a 12 s wait). The runtime stays bounded (refusal <=10 s, no new dispatch, reconciliation record) and the lease channel refuses the late effect, but an effect on a channel the platform does not govern lands late: measured as RESIDUAL_MEASURED_NOT_PASS, not claimed contained, traced to FGM-17 and to the G6 qualification. Out-of-process execution of tools with termination at the stop is a design option for FGM-17, not authorized in this cycle (PO disposition).
A registered tool that catches BaseException is likewise not stopped by the preemption; tools are registered by the platform, never by the model, whose sandbox expressions cannot catch exceptions.

Without a stop, a call closed by its deadline leaves its lease valid: a late effect of that call through the lease channel is still authorized (the lease is not revoked on deadline expiry); the outcome is reconciled as EXECUTION_UNKNOWN. Revoking or fencing on deadline is outside the closed scope of repair 2.

The C6 OutcomeReconciler is in-memory (sealed OCOR-DEV-0044 contract): the record does not survive the process; durable reconciliation storage belongs to the C6 dispatch path and G6. The default reconciler of a runtime constructed without one is private to that runtime.
A preempted worker whose native call blocks keeps its daemon thread until that call returns; a tool blocking forever holds one thread for the life of the process.

The lease time window is still evaluated at the caller-supplied 'at' instant (0047 contract unchanged); the dispatch and refusal times of the reconciliation record use the local UTC clock, not a TrustedClock.

The lease is still the in-process CapabilityLease, not the signed single-use record of LLD v1.1 section 1.4; only stop_epoch is added. The stop is detected at dispatch and by 10 ms supervision polling, not pushed.
ToolCallRuntime is still not invoked by other ocor-runtime modules (INFO-C classification); G6 qualification (BA-08, NFR-047, FGM-17) depends on it.
